system/boot_logos/spm_boot_logos.sprite..blockNote:
Sprite map of the boot logo scene $FB: 2 animations, 2 sprite-groups, 51 parts. scene_meta_00FB loads it ($018F bytes) to $7E4000 as the actor spriteset; sFB_boot_logo selects the animations with StageSpriteLoop and plays them with AnimLoop. Colours: pal_boot_logos (80 colours, OBJ palettes 0 to 4).

=== ANIMATIONS ===

- #00 sprite_set_000004: one frame, hold $3B (60 ticks), sprite_group_000010 = the second logo (Enix): box 122 x 156 px, 35 parts.
- #01 sprite_set_00000A: one frame, hold $3B (60 ticks), sprite_group_000112 = the first logo: box 96 x 48 px, 16 parts.

=== FORMAT ===

A sprite map file has three layers (same format as the spriteset_* files, see spriteset_freedan):
- Pointer table (the first label): one word per animation index. The engine reads entry $28 of the actor (UpdateActorAnimation: table + 2 x $28), then the frame record $2A x 4 inside that list.
- Sprite-set (frame list): 4-byte records < hold, &sprite_group >, closed by a hidden $FFFF. A frame is shown for hold + 1 ticks.
- Sprite-group: 12 header bytes, the part count, then 7-byte sprite-parts. Bytes 0-3 are the X extents (left, right) and Y extents (above, below) of the frame box; UpdateActorAnimation loads them into $18/$1C and $1A/$1E and swaps each pair for a flipped actor. Bytes 4-7 are a tile-unit box (X offset, Y offset, width and height in 16-pixel units) read by PlayerAttackHitTest and the solid-rectangle COP handlers; bytes 8-11 are the body box (X offset, width, Y offset, height in pixels, signed offsets) read by CombatCollision and the interaction collision code.
- Sprite-part < size, x, x', y, y', tile word >: size 0 = 8 x 8, 1 = 16 x 16 (the OAM size bit); x and y are offsets inside the extent box, x' and y' the offsets used when the actor is H / V flipped (x + x' = box width - part width); the tile word is an OAM word (bit 8 name table, bits 9-11 palette, bits 12-13 priority, $4000 H flip, $8000 V flip) that the engine XORs with the actor's attribute word $0E.

=== BOXES ===

Every group of this file carries the engine's default boxes ($F8 $F0 $01 $01 and $F8 $10 $F0 $10): the same eight bytes are in all 85 groups of spm_boot_logos, spm_title_actors, spm_darkspace_sprites and spm_overworld_sprites. A logo has no use for them. The first audit of this file (I055) called these eight bytes 'nothing reads'; they are the two collision boxes (PlayerAttackHitTest, CombatCollision).

partNotes.sprite_set_000004: Animation #00: one frame, hold $3B (60 ticks), the second logo (Enix). sFB_boot_logo plays it for 2 passes (StageSpriteLoop #00, #02).
partNotes.sprite_set_00000A: Animation #01: one frame, hold $3B (60 ticks), the first logo. sFB_boot_logo plays it for 2 passes (StageSpriteLoop #01, #02).
partNotes.sprite_group_000010: Second logo (Enix): extents 58 + 64 = 122 px wide, 92 + 64 = 156 px tall, 35 parts, all 16 x 16. Parts 00-0F are a 4 x 4 block (tile words $01xx / $03xx = OBJ palettes 0 and 1: palette 1 for the upper two rows, palette 0 for the lower two), parts 10-17 a 4 x 2 block below it on palette 2 ($05xx), parts 18-22 a row of 11 at the bottom (y = $8C) on palette 4 ($09xx), 6 to 12 px apart. Palettes 0 to 2 are the ones the boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers animate.
partNotes.sprite_group_000112: First logo: extents 48 + 48 = 96 px wide, 16 + 32 = 48 px tall, 16 parts of 16 x 16 in rows of 6, 6 and 4 (tile words $07C0-$07CA, $07E0-$07EA and $0708-$070E).

system/boot_logos/sFB_boot_logo.asm.blockNote:
Boot logo sequence actor - scene $FB master controller (the first scene of the game). Scene $FB is entered TWICE at power-on and shows one logo per visit; the second logo then hands over to the title screen scene $FC.

=== SEQUENCE ===

1. BootLogoInit (both visits): sets displayModeFlags bit 14 (no reader found, OQ-I034-1), clears colour 0 of the palette staging buffer, enables FastROM (MEMSEL = $01), puts only the sprite layer on the main screen (TM = $10, bit 4 = OBJ; no BG is shown), masks the joypad, then reads STAT78 bit 4: 0 = 60 Hz NTSC continues, 1 = 50 Hz PAL jumps to BootLogoPalLockout.
2. First visit (event flag $10 clear): nudge the actor Y -16, play sprite animation #01 (sprite_group_000112, a 96 x 48 logo on OBJ palette 3) for 2 passes of 60 ticks = 120 ticks, set event flag $10, QueueMapChange to scene $FB itself, Die.
3. Second visit (flag set): BootLogoSecondPhase plays animation #00 (sprite_group_000010, the Enix logo: an emblem with a wordmark under it, OBJ palettes 0, 1, 2 and 4) for 120 ticks, clears flag $10 and queues scene $FC (title screen), Die.
Event flag $10 is not one of the flags the scene load zeroes (only $00 to $0F are), which is why it survives the reload; it is cleared again at the end because the South Cape church scripts (sc08_*) use the same flag.

The three boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers are spawned by the scene's thinker list in both visits and run the Enix logo's palette cycle on OBJ palettes 0, 1 and 2, i.e. only the second logo (see boot_logo_enix_palette_obj0).

=== PAL LOCKOUT ===

A 50 Hz console never sees a logo: BootLogoPalLockout draws the region warning text (consolestring_01D9D8) on BG3 and then yields forever at SetEntryHere + RTL. The game cannot be started on a PAL console.

=== POSITION ===

The scene's actor-spawn places the actor at tile (7, 8) and InitActorFromSceneData adds 8 pixels of X for normal actors; the first NudgePosition adds another 8, so the actor ends at X = 128, the centre of the 256-pixel screen. The sprite groups are laid out around that origin. QueueMapChange's last operand $1100 is the packed camera-bounds override (InitCameraBounds).

=== SPRITES (spm_boot_logos.sprite.asm) ===

The scene's spritemap card loads spm_boot_logos ($018F bytes) to $7E4000; its two entries are the animation indexes of StageSpriteLoop: #00 = sprite_set_000004 (second logo), #01 = sprite_set_00000A (first logo). Each sprite-set is one frame record (hold $003B = 60 ticks per pass, group pointer) closed by the hidden $FFFF delimiter.
First logo, sprite_group_000112: 96 x 48 px, 16 parts of 16 x 16 in rows of 6, 6 and 4, all OBJ palette 3.
Second logo, sprite_group_000010: 122 x 156 px, 35 parts: a 4 x 4 block (64 x 64) on OBJ palette 1 (upper two rows) and 0 (lower two rows), a 4 x 2 block below it on palette 2, and a row of 11 parts 12 px apart on palette 4. Palettes 0 to 2 are the ones the boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers animate; palette 4 is static.
The format (pointer table, frame list, group header with its two collision boxes, 7-byte parts) is described in the spm_boot_logos block note. The palettes come from pal_boot_logos (80 colours, OBJ palettes 0 to 4, loaded at CGRAM colour 128). The second logo is the Enix logo (its palette cycle is the three boot_logo_enix_palette_obj* thinkers); which company the first logo belongs to was not checked against the tile art.

=== NOTES ===

The joypad mask in the ROM is $FFFC (db-us/transforms.json rewrites $FFF0 to $FFFC for this block), which hides every pad bit including Start and Select, so no logo can be skipped. The old header said TM = $10 puts BG1 on the main screen and that the mask is $FFF0; TM bit 4 is the OBJ layer and the shipped mask is $FFFC.

system/dark_space/sE6_gaia.asm.blockNote:
Dark Space / Gaia hub (scene $E6, the room reached from the Dark Space portals and from the diary menu's load) plus a shared character-transformation library (Bank 08, 579499-587528; GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle in Bank 09, 630928-630997). The same spawn list is also used by scene $09, which has no scene-meta entry. scene_meta_00E6 loads spm_darkspace_sprites ($0579 bytes) and plays track $16 (bgm_space_beyond_time).

=== STRUCTURE ===

DarkSpaceMainInit spawns three children with SpawnAfter: FireflySpawnerLoop, GaiaNpcSprite and GaiaVoiceSparkle. SpawnAfter inserts each new actor right after the parent, so the main actor's $06 link ends up on the LAST one spawned, the voice sparkle (the old notes called it the Gaia NPC link). Every 'LDY $06 / STA $0024, Y' below is therefore the voice sparkle's on / off switch ($FFFF = on, 0 = off), not an NPC interaction lock.
It then validates globalScriptIndex ($0AAC: the room variant, written by the portal actor or restored by the diary load; 4 or more becomes 0), keeps it in $0AB2 (saved with the game, restored by the diary menu), clears $0AAC and switch-cases to a layout: 0 DS_LayoutBasic (Gaia only), 1 DS_LayoutTransform (statues chosen by characterForm), 2 DS_LayoutAbility (ability orb chosen by the scene), 3 DS_LayoutSpecial (sets $0AAC = 1 and runs layout 1; this is the pyramid's Dark Space, where GaiaHint_AuraItem tests $0AAC and gives the Aura item).
Every room polls BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles zones (x1, y1, x2, y2 in tiles): Gaia (7,8)-(9,9) = GaiaDialogueEntry, left statue (3,A)-(5,B), right statue (B,A)-(D,B), exit (5,D)-(B,F) = DarkSpaceExit. Each room has a wait state (the player is still standing in a zone: nothing happens, so a dialogue cannot retrigger) and an active state that dispatches the zones; the *Wait / *TileWait pairs and the loc_ labels after them are these two states.
The called scripts (GaiaDialogueEntry, the *TransformDialogue routines) are entered with CallNear and end with RestoreSavedPtr, which returns to the room loop.

=== EXIT ===

DarkSpaceExit masks the joypad, hides the player ($10 |= $2000), puts this actor on him, plays SFX $0C on both channels and the dissolve animation $1C of spriteset_enemies once, waits 30 ticks (WaitByte #1D), then fills the warp words: sceneNext = $0B12 (the scene the player warped from, saved by ExecuteWarp), player spawn X = $0B08 x 16 and Y = ($0B0C + 2) x 16 (the source warp rectangle's tile position), facing 3 and the packed camera window $0B10 / $0B11 -> warpScrollParams. gfxCacheIdxB = $0101 is the transition speed (exit and enter 1), gfxCacheIdxA = $0002 is exit effect 2 = mosaic, enter effect 0 = fade. The old notes called the destination a camera position and $0101 a brightness fade.

=== GAIA DIALOGUE ===

GaiaDialogueEntry: 6-tick pause (WaitByte #05), voice sparkle on, first visit (event flag $DC) the intro text, then GaiaHealAndHints. If HP < max it prints the 'hurt' text and writes hpToHeal = 40; UpdateHUD turns that request into +1 HP every 8 frames (SFX $0D) until HP = max (the loop yields until then). The hint is chosen by the position of the source scene in GaiaHintSceneTable (34 scenes, one GaiaHint_xx handler each; 21 of them have no text and go straight to the save prompt). GaiaSavePrompt: 'Record what's happened so far?' (DialogueOptions: entry 0 = cancel, 1 = first option, 2 = second option). Record = SaveGameState_Scene for the active slot ($0D8C), SFX $29, 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then 'Continue your journey?': Yes (entry 1) = GaiaThenGo, 'Then go.', returns to the room; No (entry 2) = GaiaThenRest, 'Then rest a while.', fades to track $0E (bgm_longing_for_the_past) and the actor yields forever. GaiaThenGo and GaiaThenRest are named after the answers 'Then go.' and 'Then rest a while.'; each is reached from two prompts (they were first called GaiaDontRecord and GaiaContinueJourney after the first prompt only, which made them look swapped for the second).

=== FORMS AND ABILITIES ===

characterForm ($0AD4): 0 Will, 1 Freedan, 2 Shadow. A statue dialogue writes a Transform_* routine into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000 / $0002, $0008 = 0) and sets playerFlags $0800; the player then plays it (player body entry #05, the transformation frames), the routine sets characterForm and DarkSpaceRestoreControl clears $0800 and sends the player back to PlayerIdleEntry. The Shadow statue needs event flag $B4, whose only writer is daC8_neil (the Neil reunion in the Dao dormitory; the old header said it is unlocked at Ankor Wat); first Freedan visit flag $F7, first Shadow visit flag $DD.
The Transform_* routines are a shared library: Transform_WillToShadow is entered from sE5_epilogue, pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and btE4_kara; Transform_ShadowToWill from pyDD_mummy_queen, gw8A_sand_fanger, mu67_vampires, sg55_viper, ir29_castoth and pyCD_jackal; Transform_FreedanToWill from sg55_mystic_statue, ir29_transform, ir1C_lily, ec13_lily, pyCD_jackal and mu67_bomb (13 files in all).
AbilitySceneTable has 6 entries of (scene, abilityBitmask bit): $15 Psycho Dash $01, $62 Psycho Slider $02, $86 Spin Dash $04, $42 Dark Friar $10, $A7 Aura Barrier $20, $B8 Earthquaker $40, ended by $00. The low nibble holds the Will abilities, the high nibble the Freedan abilities; the old header called byte 1 'ability index + statue type'. The table position is the ability index used by table_08EB8F (names) and table_08EBD3 (descriptions) through globalScriptIndex. DS_LayoutAbility shows the orb for the current scene (BG change $86 and orb at (64,109) for a Will ability, $8B and (64,84) for a Freedan ability); AbilityOrbActor dies when the bit is already in abilityBitmask, otherwise waits for the player at the statue zone, turns him into the form that can use it (Will for the low nibble, Freedan for the high nibble) with LookupAbilityForm, ORs the bit in, plays the orb flight, fanfare (track $18) and the two texts.

=== SPRITES (spm_darkspace_sprites) ===

Animation #00 (4 frames, hold $63 then $0C x 3) is GaiaNpcSprite; #01 to #03 are the three sparkle variants of GaiaVoiceSparkle; #0A (32 frames of hold 0, a 16 x 16 spark alternating with an 8 x 8 tile) is the ability orb. #04 to #09 are not selected by this file (#04 to #06 are 8 x 8 effect tiles, #07 to #09 a 32 x 32 figure of 16 x 16 parts); the spm_darkspace_sprites block note lists all eleven animations. FireflyParticle and DarkSpaceExit use spriteset_enemies.

=== NOT REFERENCED ===

No reference was found in extracted/ for: DS_AuraItemRoom and its handlers, AuraItemInteraction and its helpers (with dialogstring_08EFEF / 08F003 / 08F060), DarkSpaceAmbientParticle, the code at loc_08DA6B / loc_08DA77 (after an unconditional BRA), and the unused hint strings dialogstring_08DEC6, 08E066, 08E0C7, 08E109, 08E19C, 08E261, 08E2B9 and 08E615.

=== CORRECTIONS ===

Replaced claims: byte 1 of AbilitySceneTable is an ability bit, not an index with a statue nibble; the continue prompt's Yes / No were described the other way round; $06 is the voice sparkle, not the Gaia NPC, and $24 is its voice switch; 'Unmask D-pad and face buttons' ($0F00) is the D-pad only; hpToHeal 40 is a heal request (not 'damage flash ticks'); warpDestX / warpDestY and the $0B08-$0B12 values are the player's spawn position and source scene, not a camera; GaiaNpcSprite loops an idle animation (it is not a single frame); the Shadow flag $B4 is set by Neil, not at Ankor Wat; 'spriteset #05 (transformation frames)' is player body entry #05 and the 'transformation spriteset' of the exit effect is spriteset_enemies; Transform_ShadowToFreedan uses SetEntryHereAndYield, not SetEntryExit.

Which art animations #00 to #05 draw (which party member) was not checked.

=== FORMAT ===

A sprite map file has three layers (same format as the spriteset_* files, see spriteset_freedan):
- Pointer table (the first label): one word per animation index. The engine reads entry $28 of the actor (UpdateActorAnimation: table + 2 x $28), then the frame record $2A x 4 inside that list.
- Sprite-set (frame list): 4-byte records < hold, &sprite_group >, closed by a hidden $FFFF. A frame is shown for hold + 1 ticks.
- Sprite-group: 12 header bytes, the part count, then 7-byte sprite-parts. Bytes 0-3 are the X extents (left, right) and Y extents (above, below) of the frame box; UpdateActorAnimation loads them into $18/$1C and $1A/$1E and swaps each pair for a flipped actor. Bytes 4-7 are a tile-unit box (X offset, Y offset, width and height in 16-pixel units) read by PlayerAttackHitTest and the solid-rectangle COP handlers; bytes 8-11 are the body box (X offset, width, Y offset, height in pixels, signed offsets) read by CombatCollision and the interaction collision code.
- Sprite-part < size, x, x', y, y', tile word >: size 0 = 8 x 8, 1 = 16 x 16 (the OAM size bit); x and y are offsets inside the extent box, x' and y' the offsets used when the actor is H / V flipped (x + x' = box width - part width); the tile word is an OAM word (bit 8 name table, bits 9-11 palette, bits 12-13 priority, $4000 H flip, $8000 V flip) that the engine XORs with the actor's attribute word $0E.
Every group of this file carries the engine's default boxes ($F8 $F0 $01 $01 and $F8 $10 $F0 $10): the same eight bytes are in all 85 groups of spm_boot_logos, spm_title_actors, spm_darkspace_sprites and spm_overworld_sprites.

system/world_map/WorldMapController.asm.blockNote:
World map controller (scene $FE actor, Bank 03, 238321-239290). The scene is a Mode 7 map; this file runs the arrival zoom, the destination menu, the companion dots, the route playback and the dive into the destination scene.

=== HOW A TRIP STARTS ===

Both kinds of trip arrive through CheckSceneTransition / ExecuteSceneTransition, which see a nonzero $0D52/$0D53 and then move $0D52 -> $0D54 (worldMapPlayerX), $0652 -> $0D6C, sceneNext -> $0D6E and sceneCurrent -> $0D6F, and switch to scene $FE:
- Menu trip: the exit actor in a town or dungeon entrance (overworld_exit) writes $0D60 := 0 and runs COP StageWorldMapChoice (start X, start Y, choice id). The choice id in $0D58 selects a menu in world_map_options.
- Scripted trip: an NPC departure script (13 of them, e.g. ec0A_kara, wa79_neil, daC8_neil) fills the party array, runs COP StageWorldMapMove (start X, start Y, 0, route id) and has already queued the destination with QueueMapChange. StageWorldMapMove clears $0D58, so there is no menu.

=== STATE BLOCK $0D52-$0D6F ===

| Address | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| $0D52 | staged start X; nonzero = a world-map entry is pending (moved to $0D54 and cleared on arrival) |
| $0D54 / $0D56 | worldMapPlayerX / Y: start position on the 1024 x 1024 map |
| $0D58 | choice id (0 = none). The low 5 bits index world_map_options |
| $0D5A | route id (0 = none). Index into world_map_route_table, set by COP #65 / #67 |
| $0D5C | route subroutine return pointer (0 = none) |
| $0D5E | written by COP #65 / #67 (always 0), never read |
| $0D60-$0D6A | party array: six words of spm_overworld_sprites animation indices. $0D60 is the leader, $0D62-$0D6A are up to five companions, 0 = empty |
| $0D6C | deferred $0652 (scroll parameters of the queued scene change) |
| $0D6E | destination scene (low byte); a scripted trip gets it from ExecuteSceneTransition, a menu trip from DeferSceneTransition |
| $0D6F | scene being left (the start name is looked up with it) |

ClearWorldMapState zeroes $0D52-$0D6D (14 words, CPY #$001C), so $0D6E/$0D6F survive the trip.

=== MODE 7 PARAMETERS THE CONTROLLER DRIVES ===

Mode7PerspectiveInit (scene thinker, see mode7_perspective) sets the global words $B8 := $0400, $B6 := 0, $BC := 0 and the centre $CA/$CC := ($0D54, $0D56). Per frame it turns them into the M7A-M7D HDMA tables:
- $B8 is the divisor at the top scanline: smaller = zoomed out, larger = zoomed in ($80 is about 1:1).
- $B6 is how much the divisor grows per scanline: 0 = flat map, larger = stronger perspective.
- $BC is the rotation index (512 steps per turn). Route steps change it, so the map turns during a trip. The old comments called it elevation.
- $CA/$CC are the world X/Y (map centre). cameraTargetX/Y follow as centre - ($80, $70).

=== TIMELINE ===

1. WorldMapController (WorldMapControllerEntry): characterForm := 0, two palette-reset thinkers (bundle $0B: Will's normal sprite colours, CGRAM $81-$8F), ClearAllWramFlags, mask the buttons, spawn ArrivalAndTravelSetup as a child (flags $3800). With no choice id it dies here; otherwise it gives the child animScratch2 |= $0804, saves DeferSceneTransition with SetSavedPtr and runs world_map_options[choice & $1F] (menu and handler).
2. ArrivalAndTravelSetup, 44 ticks: places itself (the leader's dot) at the start position, centres the camera, then each tick adds the TickGravity delta (always negative: -$20 rising to about -2) to $B8. The divisor falls from $0400 to about $34 (hand-computed), a zoom-out from 8x in to a wide view.
3. Menu trips only: wait 16 ticks (WaitByte #0F), spawn WorldMapSplitEffect, then poll $0D5A every frame (RTL = try again next frame) while the menu is open. Choosing Quit leaves it at 0: the handler has already queued the scene you came from and DeferSceneTransition just dies, so this actor idles until the scene changes.
4. Tilt phase (TiltPhaseStart), 93 ticks: shows the start-area name (see world_map_scene_names), adds the TickGravity delta ((t * (t >> 1)) >> 7, growing) to $B6 and 1 to $B8. $B6 ends at about $03F0, so the flat map tilts into a strong perspective view. Then the name is cleared ($00DA := 0).
5. Companion dots: the party array is scanned from $0D62, N companions pick entry N of companion_formation_tables, and one CompanionDotMovement actor per companion is spawned. RouteAnimationEngine is spawned and this actor becomes the leader's dot.
6. RouteAnimationEngine plays the route bytes (see world_map_route_table): X, Y and rotation steps change $CA/$CC/$BC.
7. RouteEndHandler: dots die, the destination name shows for 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), $B6 falls by $10 per frame until the map is flat again (Start skips everything), then the deferred sceneNext/$0652 are restored and the controller dives: $B8 grows by an increasing delta, a zoom-in while the scene exit transition runs.

=== SPRITES (spm_overworld_sprites) ===

The spritemap (scene_meta_00FE, $1238 bytes, gfx_overworld_actors, palette pal_overworld_sprites at colour $90) has 14 animations; the spm_overworld_sprites block note lists them. The leader and companion dots use the animation index from the party array as actor field $28.
- 0-5: 4-frame cycles (hold 7), one per party slot value (art identity not checked). 6: one 16 x 16 part in 4 frames.
- 7-A: four 5-frame sets. wa79_neil fills the party array with 7, 8, 9, A for the Watermia to Euro leg (menu handlers set only $0D60 := 7), so these look like the pieces of one vehicle (not checked at runtime).
- B: 3 frames of hold 1, a 79 x 48 px box of 24 parts, used as the leader by daC8_neil (Dao to Over Babel). C: the same box with 27 parts, no writer found. D: 4 frames of hold 9, 48-64 x 64 px, used as the leader by wa78_men (Watermia to South Cape).

=== KEY ROUTINES ===

- DeferSceneTransition: callback after the menu handler; keeps the queued scene out of the way while the route plays.
- ArrivalAndTravelSetup: arrival zoom, menu wait, tilt phase, dot formation, route launch; then runs as the leader's dot.
- CompanionDotMovement: one companion dot (also the shared dot loop).
- RouteAnimationEngine: interpreter for the world_map_route_table bytes. RouteEndHandler: end-of-route name, untilt and dive.
- LookupMapName: scene id -> name string pointer.

tables/spriteset_freedan.asm.blockNote:
Freedan player spriteset (Bank 0E, 950272-969435): every frame the player can show in form 1. 76 animations ($00-$4B), 353 frame records, 186 sprite groups, 2147 sub-sprites (at most 14 per group). Chosen by body_table[1] (art free_sprites_1AC000); SetActorBody copies the table pointer and bank into the actor ($7F0006, $7F0008). The player scripts pick the animation with StagePlayerSprite and friends; the numbering is shared with spriteset_will and spriteset_shadow.

=== FORMAT (the same in every spriteset_* file) ===

- Table: one word pointer per animation index ($28), relative to the spriteset bank.
- Frame list (sprite-set): 4-byte records < hold, &sprite_group >. A frame is shown for hold + 1 ticks. The list ends with a hidden $FFFF word that the extraction does not show (a list of n records is 4n + 2 bytes; this was checked for all 76 lists by label spacing and in the ROM). Any negative word works, AdvanceSpriteAnim tests the sign. docs/structs-reference.md says the terminator is $0000: that is wrong.
- Sprite group: 13-byte header, then 7-byte sub-sprites.
  - Header bytes 0-1: X extents (left, right); bytes 2-3: Y extents (top, bottom). UpdateActorAnimation loads them into $18/$1C and $1A/$1E (screen culling) and swaps each pair for a flipped actor.
  - Bytes 4-7: a tile-unit box read at metaspritePtr+0..3 by PlayerAttackHitTest (the attack's hit area) and by the solid-rectangle COP handlers (cop_handlers_collision): X offset and Y offset (the code ORs $FF00 into them, so they are always negative), width and height in 16-pixel units (shifted left four times). Default $F8 $F0 $01 $01 = a 16 x 16 box at (-8, -16).
  - Bytes 8-11: the body box, read at metaspritePtr+4..7 by CombatCollision (RunCombatCollision) and the interaction collision code: X offset (signed; mirrored for an H-flipped actor), width in pixels, Y offset (signed), height in pixels. Default $F8 $10 $F0 $10 = 16 x 16 at (-8, -16); some groups have other values.
  - Byte 12: the number of sub-sprites (equal to the real count in all 186 groups).
- Sub-sprite < size, x, x', y, y', tile word >: size 0 = 8x8, 1 = 16x16 (the OAM size bit); x / y is the offset inside the extent box and x' / y' the mirrored offset used for a flipped actor (x + x' = total width - size, checked by hand on three sub-sprites); the tile word is a normal OAM word (tile low byte, bit 8 name table, bits 9-11 palette, 12-13 priority, $4000 H flip, $8000 V flip).
- The same group is used by several frames and animations (353 records name 186 groups): animations $04-$07 reuse the four idle groups of $00-$03.

Tile art: the tile byte of a sub-sprite selects 32-byte tiles in free_sprites_1AC000; the player art is DMAed as the frames change (sprite_composition).

=== PLAYER ANIMATION NUMBERS ===

See the part note of the table for the index map. The previous header claimed 'Dark Friar cast poses': the ability cast in attack_ability_system stages the ordinary attack animations $36-$39, no separate Dark Friar animation was identified.
